question: Should OpenClaw add a built-in response-level tool confirmation gate, and what deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules should decide allow, require-confirm, deny, and timeout behavior?
rationale: Source inspection proves the requested gate is missing, but the permanent behavior defines a new core authorization boundary and config contract that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design core confirmation gate
options.body: Approve a maintainer-led core design with disabled-by-default config, deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules, explicit approve/deny/timeout behavior, and regression coverage around existing plugin and exec approvals.

options.title: Keep plugin-only approvals
options.body: Leave core behavior unchanged and require operators or plugins to implement contextual approvals through before_tool_call.requireApproval, accepting that no built-in same-response confirmation gate exists.

options.title: Fold into broader policy model
options.body: Wait for related action-level deny, response-gate, HITL interrupt, and MCP consent work to settle into one authorization model before adding a new config surface.

recommendation.title: Design core confirmation gate
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-led core design with disabled-by-default config, deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules, explicit approve/deny/timeout behavior, and regression coverage around existing plugin and exec approvals.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans security defaults, config compatibility, and the core agent execution loop, and prior review already routed it to core product/security design.
